bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `src/backtrace.c:65` in `each_backtrace()` on the exact staged 2477-byte Ruby witness. The harness NUL-terminates that file and `mrb_load_string()` enters project code at `mrb_load_string_cxt()`, where `strlen(s)` derives the byte length passed into the mruby load/parse chain before the script is executed. On the crashing path the saved stack shows execution in `BasicObject#instance_eval` (`f_instance_eval -> exec_irep -> cipush`). `f_instance_eval` compiles an attacker-controlled eval string into a new proc, and `vm.c:737` repurposes the current callinfo for that proc by setting `ci->pc = p->body.irep->iseq` before any instruction in the new irep has executed. The subsequent `cipush()` computes the current call depth and finds `size > MRB_CALL_LEVEL_MAX`, so it raises `mrb->stack_err` before `ci->pc` is advanced past the first instruction. Exception setup then preserves a backtrace. `each_backtrace()` allocates stack local `struct backtrace_location loc` without initialization, computes `pc = &ci->pc[-1]`, and subtracts `irep->iseq` to derive `idx`. Because `ci->pc` still equals `irep->iseq`, `pc` points one instruction before the bytecode array and `idx` becomes out of range. Vulnerable `mrb_debug_get_position()` only initializes `*lp` and `*fp` inside `if (irep && pc < irep->ilen) { ... }`; with this out-of-range `idx`, it falls through to `return FALSE` and leaves both output parameters untouched. `each_backtrace()` immediately evaluates `if (loc.lineno == -1)`, so the branch reads the uninitialized `loc.lineno` field and triggers the saved MSAN report. The staged patch fixes that exact obligation by setting `*lp = -1; *fp = NULL` on all failure exits from `mrb_debug_get_position()`.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-controlled Ruby source by converting the NUL-terminated script buffer to a byte length and forwarding that `s,len` pair into mruby's load/parse path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 2477-byte Ruby script that the harness NUL-terminates and passes into `mrb_load_string()`. `mrb_load_string_cxt()` is the first mruby project statement that consumes that buffer: it calls `strlen(s)` to derive the byte length and forwards the same `s` pointer plus that length into `mrb_load_nstring_cxt()`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: Concrete uninitialized object named by the MSAN origin. `loc` is a stack `struct backtrace_location` whose fields are only defined if later code stores through `&loc.lineno` and `&loc.filename`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: MemorySanitizer says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `loc` in the `each_backtrace` stack frame. The report points to function line 34; the concrete local declaration is line 39.
tainted_value_origin.note: The vulnerable path relies on `mrb_debug_get_position()` to fill `loc.lineno` and `loc.filename`, but that callee can return without writing either output parameter.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. `each_backtrace()` branches on `loc.lineno` even though the preceding `mrb_debug_get_position()` call may have returned without storing through `&loc.lineno`.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `src/backtrace.c:65:9` in `each_backtrace()` and attributes the poisoned origin to the stack allocation of `loc` in the same function.

root_cause.description: Root cause. When the caller supplies an out-of-range bytecode index, the outer `if (irep && pc < irep->ilen)` is false, so the vulnerable function reaches `return FALSE` without initializing the caller-provided `lp` and `fp` outputs.
root_cause.note: On the crashing path `each_backtrace()` passes `&loc.lineno` and `&loc.filename`. Because step 10's `idx` is outside `irep->ilen`, the function returns `FALSE` with both outputs untouched, so the uninitialized contents of step 8's stack local remain live. The staged patch adds `*lp = -1; *fp = NULL;` before the final return to satisfy that missing initialization obligation.

parser_admitted.condition: The staged crashing run reaches `mrb_load_exec -> mrb_top_run` rather than any early parse/codegen return, so the witness passed mruby parsing and entered actual script execution before the `instance_eval` recursion and backtrace path.

fine_trace.note: First project consumer of the staged NUL-terminated witness. `strlen(s)` materializes the byte length from the attacker buffer and forwards the same `s,len` pair into mruby's load/parse chain.

On the crashing path the saved stack reaches `f_instance_eval`. This argument decode extracts the string source for that `instance_eval` invocation, so attacker-controlled Ruby data from the witness becomes the nested eval input `s,len`.

fine_trace.code: proc = create_proc_from_string(mrb, s, len, mrb_nil_value(), file, line);
fine_trace.note: Compiles the `instance_eval` string from step 2 into a new Ruby proc `proc`. That proc is the irep whose callinfo will immediately be repurposed in the VM.

Repurposes the current callinfo for step 3's proc. The macro stores `ci->proc = p` and initializes `ci->pc = p->body.irep->iseq`, so the frame now points at the very first bytecode instruction before any instruction in that proc has executed.

When the nested `instance_eval` path asks for another callinfo, `cipush()` materializes the current call depth as `size`. This is the value immediately checked against `MRB_CALL_LEVEL_MAX` on the crashing path.

The depth check is true, so mruby raises `mrb->stack_err` before `cipush()` reallocates or pushes a new callinfo. The current frame from step 4 therefore still has `ci->pc == irep->iseq` when exception handling begins.

Exception setup snapshots a backtrace for the raised stack error. This transfers control into `packed_backtrace()` / `each_backtrace()` while the top Ruby frame is still the just-entered proc from step 4.

Allocates the per-frame backtrace record on the stack without initialization. MSAN's origin names this local `loc` in `each_backtrace()` as the source of the uninitialized bytes later read at the sink.

For the current frame from step 4, `ci->pc` still equals `irep->iseq`, so `pc = &ci->pc[-1]` points one instruction before the bytecode array. Subtracting `irep->iseq` turns that pointer into an out-of-range `idx`, and `each_backtrace()` asks `mrb_debug_get_position()` to fill the still-uninitialized `loc` fields using that invalid index.

Because step 9 passed an out-of-range `idx`, the outer `if (irep && pc < irep->ilen)` is false and the vulnerable function reaches `return FALSE` without storing through `lp` or `fp`. Step 8's `loc.lineno` and `loc.filename` therefore remain whatever uninitialized stack bytes they held before the call.

Sink. `each_backtrace()` immediately branches on `loc.lineno` after step 10 returned without writing it. This is the first observed use of the poisoned stack field, and it is the exact line reported by the staged MemorySanitizer trace.

allocation_context.note: The MSAN origin says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `loc` in the `each_backtrace` stack frame at line 34; the concrete local declaration is `struct backtrace_location loc;` at line 39.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch modifies `src/debug.c:mrb_debug_get_position()` to set `*lp = -1; *fp = NULL;` on every failure exit. That directly closes the missing initialization path used in fine-trace step 10, so `each_backtrace()` no longer reads stale `loc` fields when `idx` is out of range.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: Parsed from the staged `sanitizer_trace.txt` / `default_crash_trace.txt`, cross-checked against the staged vulnerable source tree in `gt_results/arvo_56554/_work/src/mruby`, the staged `patch.diff`, `poc`, and `reproduction_report.json`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. Fine-trace step 11 is the exact `each_backtrace()` branch at `src/backtrace.c:65` named by both staged MSAN traces.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. MSAN's origin names the concrete stack object `loc` from step 8, and step 10 is the helper failure path that leaves that same object's fields unwritten before step 11 reads them.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack `each_backtrace -> packed_backtrace -> mrb_keep_backtrace -> mrb_exc_raise -> cipush -> exec_irep -> f_instance_eval -> mrb_load_exec` matches the rebuilt source chain from the nested `instance_eval` proc setup through backtrace construction.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. Step 8 allocates uninitialized `loc`, step 9 passes `&loc.lineno`/`&loc.filename` to `mrb_debug_get_position()` using an out-of-range `idx`, step 10 returns without writing either output, and step 11 is the first observed read of `loc.lineno`.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: Stage 01 preserved only the vulnerable run and the fixed image was unavailable, so `patch_resolves` is grounded in the staged source diff rather than a fixed-build rerun.

poc.trigger: Running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_56554 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` on the staged `poc` reproduces `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `each_backtrace` with stack `each_backtrace -> packed_backtrace -> mrb_keep_backtrace`.

format.name: Exact staged Ruby source witness
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 2477-byte Ruby script staged at `poc` (sha256 `22383d3a7d56f6adf37c613c1f17807e68b85e5775b0bae64ff855660447dde6`). The harness NUL-terminates that file and passes it to `mrb_load_string()`. In the reproduced vulnerable build this exact script reaches `BasicObject#instance_eval`, exceeds `MRB_CALL_LEVEL_MAX` in `cipush()`, and then triggers the backtrace-building uninitialized read at `src/backtrace.c:65`. No broader class of Ruby programs is claimed here.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 did not instrument the workspace. The exact Ruby-level recursion shape inside the witness is therefore kept only to the level forced by the saved stack and source: the crashing path definitely reaches `f_instance_eval` and triggers `size > MRB_CALL_LEVEL_MAX`, but no stronger dynamic claim is made.
The fixed image was unavailable and Stage 01 only preserved the vulnerable reproduction. `patch_resolves` is grounded in the staged `patch.diff` rather than an executed fixed-build rerun.
